entry_state: The separate principal-100 instrument derives its tax reversal and financing cost 9 before joining company earnings and EPS. Apple's displayed share counts and weighted averages constrain timing without identifying dates: two constructed histories satisfy selected annual, first-quarter and purchase-window constraints. The following award discussion distinguishes RSUs, net common issuance, equity changes and cash, and its grant-value/future-cost explanation continues next.
exit_state: Plan reserve capacity, earned awards, delivered common shares and expense are distinct. The performance schedule derives units from an evidenced percentile and absolute-return cap, then applies employment and dividend-equivalent terms. Missing rank conventions and individual inputs stay unresolved. Later agreement versions are now introduced to narrow which termination and delivery rights apply.
findings: The unrecognised RSU cost and weighted recognition period cannot establish a constant annual expense or cash liability; the ownership subsection closes with linked cohorts, dates and measurements.
The plan's two-for-one full-value reserve rule yields 160 reserve shares used for 80 common shares delivered; option gross counting can deliver the same shares with different reserve use.
The performance multiplier defines the percentile scale before use and explicitly preserves the discontinuity at 25. Its interpolation slopes and examples are reconstructible.

Averaging the contractual twenty-day windows produces negative absolute return in the example even though endpoint prices rise. The return cap, surviving employment rights and cash dividend equivalents remain separate calculations.
Proxy summaries and filed forms have an unresolved applicability/timing distinction; the prose does not declare a contradiction for an identified award. No new confirmed local defect.
